title: Ingress fleet peak projections & buffer plan (2027 Q3 sweep)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet consolidates the latest observed peaks, three growth scenarios, and an actionable buffer (safety stock) plan for the public ingress fleet that serves the Hosted API. Scope: global regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west, apac-sin), all GPU families currently in production (A100-40, A100-80, H100-80), and warm-cache/kv-cache implications.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Observed 99th-percentile token rate across regions (last 30d) is ~4.2M tokens/sec aggregate.
- Near-term (Q3 2027) conservative peak projection: 6.8M tokens/sec aggregate under holiday ad-hoc growth + new partner onboarding.
- Buffer recommendation: 35% regional safety stock above projected peak (boots-on-ground GPUs + warm slices) to cover sudden partner bursts and single-region failover traffic.
- Tactical asks: +48 A100-80 GPUs across us-west/us-east FPO by 2027-12-01; enable cross-region fallback lane and prewarm policy to reduce cold-start latency and token-cost inflation during spikes.

Assumptions & data sources:
- Baseline: rolling 30d telemetry from ingress-proxy and token-metering pipeline (sum of client_token_count per 1s buckets).
- Growth scenarios are driven by: (1) organic product growth + 15% q/q, (2) two prioritized enterprise customers onboarded in Q3 (adds bursty 400k tokens/s each), (3) a marketing campaign spike (one-time weekend multiplier x1.6).
- Average tokens per request: 420; median request length 110 tokens.
- Effective throughput per GPU: measured steady-state generation throughput (A100-80: ~95k tokens/s for gen-heavy workloads, H100-80: ~140k tokens/s for quantized 4-bit variants). We purposely use conservative 85% of measured peak when sizing (to account for tail latency and multi-tenant inefficiencies).

Projection table (aggregated):
- Observed 30d P99: 4,200,000 tokens/s aggregate.
- Scenario A (steady growth +15% q/q): 4,830,000 tokens/s.
- Scenario B (enterprise onboarding + marketing tail): 6,800,000 tokens/s.
- Scenario C (extreme one-off surge): 9,800,000 tokens/s (planning limit).

Regional split (current observed -> conservative projection for Scenario B):
- us-west: current 1.6M -> proj 2.8M tokens/s (includes partner burst).
- us-east: current 1.2M -> proj 2.0M tokens/s.
- eu-west: current 0.9M -> proj 1.1M tokens/s.
- apac-sin: current 0.5M -> proj 0.9M tokens/s.

GPU mix and capacity translation (Scenario B, conservative utilization target = 65% sustained):
- Expected peak tokens/s = 6,800,000.
- Effective tokens/s per instance at 65% util: A100-80 -> 95k * 0.65 = 61.75k; H100-80 -> 140k * 0.65 = 91k.
- If we maintain current pool composition (70% A100-80, 30% H100-80), required fleet: approx 96 A100-80 + 33 H100-80 (round up). Current pool (as of inventory report): 62 A100-80 + 20 H100-80 -> shortfall = 34 A100-80 equivalent (or 12 H100-80 replacements).

Headroom policy (recommended):
- Operational headroom target = 35% above projected peak per region. Rationale: covers partner bursts, regional failover, autoscaler reaction delays, and some capacity lost to maintenance.
- Cold-start buffer: keep 10% of GPUs in a warm-but-idle state (quick prewarm slices with KV cache primed for common prompts).
- Rapid burst lane: reserve a small cluster (3% of regional pool) that can be shifted to serve low-latency high-QPS traffic with higher priority scheduling (billing as burst credits).

Prewarm & caching considerations:
- Warm KV cache reduces per-request token churn by up to 12% on observed prompt sets for chat flows. We recommend targeted prewarm for the top 150 prompt templates (derived from analytics). Cost to maintain warm cache: ~0.9 GPU-equivalent per region for us-west/us-east at current traffic patterns.

Scaling timeline and procurement asks:
- Immediate (30 days): enable cross-region fallback routing policy; implement canary for prewarm job that seeds KV cache for top templates. (Tickets: INFRA-4721)
- 30–90 days: procure + provision 24 A100-80 to us-west, 12 A100-80 to us-east. Convert 8 low-util A100s to H100s where supported to improve throughput for quantized models. (Tickets: INFRA-4890, HW-PR-88)
- >90 days: evaluate additional H100 procurement and longer-term fleet rebalancing by cost-per-token metrics.

Cost estimate (incremental for Scenario B buffer):
- Incremental units requested: 36 A100-80 (mix described above). Approx monthly cost (reserved/capacity blended estimate): $150k/month incremental. One-time procurement/setup: estimated $28k per rack (network + k8s node config) * 3 racks = $84k.

Operational runbook (short checklist for on-call/SRE):
1) Alert threshold: when regional token ingestion > 85% of provisioned capacity for > 3 continuous minutes -> trigger surge channel and post status.
2) If autorepair/autoscaler fails, flip traffic to fallback region per priority map (us-west -> us-east).
3) During fallback events, remove prewarm-heavy workloads and enable burst lane.
4) Post-incident: run debrief and sample requests to validate KV cache hit ratio; tune prewarm templates.

Risk matrix (top 5):
- Single region hardware failure during partner burst -> mitigated by +35% headroom and cross-region fallback, residual risk moderate.
- Overprovisioning cost if projected growth doesn't materialize -> mitigated by staged procurement and convert-to-reserved only after 90d.
- Model shifts (new larger context models) increasing per-token compute -> monitor model onboarding tracker and add model-specific perf profiles in the routing table.
- Autoscaler lag under very bursty patterns -> implement shorter evaluation windows and a soft prewarm trigger based on traffic derivatives.
- KV cache priming inefficiencies -> run randomized A/B to measure hit-rate gains pre-deploy.

Open questions / items for PM/Model-Ops: 
- Which of the Q3 onboarding customers are allowed to use cross-region failover (data locality compliance)? PM to confirm (ask @Priya Desai).
- Can model-ops provide per-model effective tokens/s at both 16-bit and 4-bit quant modes for H100? This materially affects procurement choice.
- Confirm budget owner for incremental reserved capacity vs on-demand burst credits.

Appendix A — quick reference table (Scenario B):
Region | Projected peak (tokens/s) | Headroom @35% | Provisioned tokens/s needed | Equivalent A100-80 (65% util)
us-west | 2,800,000 | 980,000 | 3,780,000 | 61.2 (~62)
us-east | 2,000,000 | 700,000 | 2,700,000 | 43.7 (~44)
eu-west | 1,100,000 | 385,000 | 1,485,000 | 24.0 (~24)
apac-sin | 900,000 | 315,000 | 1,215,000 | 19.7 (~20)
Total | 6,800,000 | 2,380,000 | 9,180,000 | 148 (~148 across regions)

Next steps / owners: 
- Emma Chen: finalize procurement plan + costs, due 2026-12-10.
- Rafael Ortiz: enable cross-region fallback policy and create canary route, due 2026-12-01.
- Priya Desai: confirm data residency allowances for partner failover and list of onboarding customers with SLAs, due 2026-11-20.

Notes: This is a working sheet meant to be iterated with SRE, Model-Ops, and Sales for confirmed partner load shapes. Replace conservative throughput factors with measured per-model numbers once model-ops provides the requested metrics.

Document history: initial draft 2026-11-12 by Emma Chen; reviewed 2026-11-20 (Rafael Ortiz), 2026-11-28 (Priya Desai).
